column1: # The Paws tavern's lore branch: buy a drink to establish continuation,
# then follow the advertised letter into the sage flow (cleak/u5-spec#238).
# Seeded rather than walked to. The walk-up form of this scenario scripted its
# way in from the town gate, and the resident walks its own schedule while
# those steps run, so the two sides arrived with it in different cells and
# every later beat compared unrelated windows (`cleak/u5-engine#22`).
# `qa/tools/reseed.py` replayed that walk once into the seed named below.
# `shops.md` §2: a shopkeeper's "conversation-contact event also reaches it
# automatically during a town schedule pass, even if the player has issued no
# Talk command", so the first Pass beside the keeper opens the overlay and the
# script drives it from there rather than issuing Talk.
# Two lotteries run here, so a row-offset difference must be re-run before it
# The entry greeting is one of four `SHOPPE.DAT` records (`shops.md` Section 8's
# entry table, tavern rows 57..60) and the sage's rumour phrasing is another
# pool. `prng.md` Section 3 seeds the two sides from the host clock at the
# intro menu, so they never draw the same row. Measured 2026-09-11: the
# original opened with `"Jolly good afternoon, mate! Welcome to The Cat's
# Lair!..."` and this engine with `"Welcome to The Cat's Lair! My name is Dr.
# Cat..."`. Those wrap to different row counts, which offsets every later beat
# even when each beat's own structure agrees exactly - as it now does.
# The greeting's length is also what decides the entry prompt's punctuation.
# Section 8.B makes the colon conditional on the finished greeting's column:
# column 0 gives `\n:`, columns 1..11 a single space and no colon, columns
# 12..15 `\n\n:`. A capture where one side shows `thee?" ` and the other `:`
# is that rule applied to two different draws, not a defect.

column4: Journey Onward on the seeded cell
